  <section v="10">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that through contemplation of the Yechidah, which awakens total self-nullification, both modes of refinement include both advantages.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">And the verse continues “for many are with me,”</t>

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two types of peace (from above downward and from below upward) must each include the quality of the other, so that the refinement of the animal soul and the world is complete.

translations.translation: And this is “And I will return in
peace,”
and likewise “He redeemed in
peace,”
peace from above downward and peace from below upward,
that the refinement of the animal soul
(“He redeemed my soul in peace”)
and likewise the refinement of the sparks in the world
(“and I will return in peace to my father’s house”)
must be in two manners,
in a way from above downward and in a way from below upward,
through which there are the two aspects
(advantages)
of peace.
And to add,
that the perfection of peace
(peace also from the term completion)
is when the peace
(in each of the two manners)
includes both advantages.
That also in the refinement that is in the way from below upward there is
(a semblance of)
the aspect of transformation,
and that also in the refinement that is in the way from above downward there is
(a semblance of)
the advantage that the refinement is from the perspective of the nature of the lower.
And this is “He redeemed my soul in peace from near to me,”
that also the aspect of “He redeemed in peace,”
which is
(generally)
the redemption of the G-dly soul from the exile of the animal soul through the revelation of light,
will have in it the advantage of “from near to me”
(near from the term closeness),
the refinement of the animal soul itself.
And likewise on the other side,
that also the refinement that is in the way of near
(war)
will be in a manner of “He redeemed in peace,”
transformation.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that through contemplation of the Yechidah, which awakens total self-nullification, both modes of refinement include both advantages.

translations.translation: And the verse continues “for many are with me,”
“for many are with me” is the reason
(for)
“He redeemed my soul in peace from near to me,”
that through contemplation of the aspect of Yechidah,
through which there is awakened in him the aspect of self-nullification
[namely,
that even before the service of “He redeemed my soul in peace from near to me” and he still needs to redeem his G-dly soul from the wars of the animal soul,
he is awakened to a total self-nullification to G-dliness,
which comes from the Yechidah within him],
through this,
the refinement of the animal soul is in a manner of “He redeemed my soul in peace from near to me,”
that in each of the two modes of refinement there are both advantages.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the above to the Rebbe's father-in-law's explanation that Torah study must be felt as God's Torah, achieved through prayer, which brings peace to scholars and the world.

translations.translation: And it is possible to connect this matter with what is explained by my revered father-in-law, the Rebbe, in his maamar beginning “And all
your children [shall be] students of the L-rd, and great shall be the peace of your children,” said on Shabbos Parshas Vayeitzei 5689
(in the Kuntres of Wedding Discourses),
that the translation of the verse “And all your children etc.” is “And all your children are learned in the Torah of the L-rd, and great shall be the peace of your children.”
And he explains,
that this precise wording “learned in the Torah of the L-rd”
(even though seemingly this is not a novelty,
for everyone knows that the Torah is the Torah of the L-rd)
is,
that their Torah study is in a manner that he feels that the Torah is the Torah of the L-rd.
And he adds in the maamar,
that the explanation of “learned in the Torah of the L-rd” is,
that even though the study of Torah
(learning)
is that he understands and grasps the Torah with his intellect
(human intellect),
nevertheless,
also in his study
(intellect)
it is felt that the Torah is the Torah of the L-rd,
“learned in the Torah of the L-rd.”
And through this feeling,
also his study
(comprehension)
is in self-nullification.
And in order for Torah study to be in this manner,
it is through the prior service of prayer.
For the matter of prayer is connection and self-nullification to G-dliness.
And through Torah study in this manner
(specifically)
there is “great shall be the peace of your children” – an abundance of peace for the Torah scholars who engage in Torah,
and also an abundance of peace in the world, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, learned
from this verse that Torah scholars increase peace in the world.
